history.summary: Historic Hindu temple dedicated to Lord Vishnu near the confluence of the Indravati and Narangi rivers, about 4 km east of Chitrakote Falls. Built c. 1111 AD by Mumunda Devi (Gunda Mahadevi), queen-mother of the Chindaka Naga dynasty; an inscription in Devanagari script at the temple records a land grant to 'Lokeswar'. The Nagara-style temple with Chalukya influence is built on a saptaratha plan with an imposing curvilinear shikhara, and the sanctum holds a four-armed black-stone image of Vishnu canopied by a hooded serpent, reflecting tribal influence. Archaeologists believe it was originally a Shiva temple, later rededicated to Vishnu. Said to be the only ancient Vishnu temple in Bastar district and contemporary with the Khajuraho temples; a protected monument under the Archaeological Survey of India. (CSV town 'Jagdalpur' is wrong — the temple is at Narayanpal village, ~42 km NW of Jagdalpur; variant legends attribute construction to King Someshwar of the Nagavanshi dynasty, flagged as unverified.)

name: Narayanpal Temple
town_description: Narayanpal is a small village in Bastar district of Chhattisgarh, about 42 km northwest of Jagdalpur and roughly 4 km from the famous Chitrakote Falls. It sits at the confluence of the Indravati and Narangi rivers and grew up around its 11th-century Vishnu temple; the village itself is said to have been named after the temple's deity (originally Narayanpur). Like much of Bastar, it is a tribal-dominated rural settlement where the ancient temple remains the focal point of local religious life.
